newsitem.title: GERMANY: Only states meeting criteria can join EMU - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Only states meeting criteria can join EMU - Waigel.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Wednesday that he wanted European economic and monetary union only to go ahead with countries which meet the convergence goals set by the Maastricht treaty.
"The Euro will start only with the countries which fulfill the preconditions," Waigel was due to say in a speech. "I will not stand for a weakening of the stability criteria."

Waigel's comments were made in the text of a speech he was due to give later to the traditional Ash Wednesday meeting of his Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU).

His remarks followed mounting concerns over whether Germany itself can meet the Maastricht budget deficit goal of three percent of gross domestic product this year after unemployment jumped to a 64-year record in January of 4.66 million.
The German Finance Ministry on Tuesday rejected reports the budget deficit would climb to 3.5 percent of GDP this year, saying it stood by the government forecast of 2.9 percent.
European countries seeking to join EMU will have their 1997 performance reviewed early next year, when leaders will agree on a starting line-up for the planned 1999 launch of the euro.
